title: TrackFlow telemetry events
description: JSON Schema draft-07. Validate any event against the root; `oneOf` selects the schema by `event_type`.

envelope.description: Fields every event carries. `event_type` and `properties` are narrowed per event.

eventId.description: Unique per event; consumers deduplicate on it.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC time the event occurred at the emitter.

sessionId.description: Random id generated per browser tab session (and per script run); there is no server session.

userId.description: TinyDB user UUID; null when anonymous or the account is unknown.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this event's schema.

requestId.description: Correlates all events and logs of one HTTP request; scripts use one id per run.

product_created.title: product_created
product_created.description: We capture product_created because we need to know how fast the catalogue grows per warehouse and who is onboarding SKUs, which allows us to plan catalogue-maintenance capacity and spot warehouses that lag in onboarding.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

initial_stock.description: Always 0; stock is derived, never stored.

product_creation_rejected.title: product_creation_rejected
product_creation_rejected.description: We capture product_creation_rejected because we need to know whether operators keep trying to register duplicates or malformed products, which allows us to decide whether the creation form needs duplicate detection or clearer guidance.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

rejected_fields.description: Names of fields that failed validation.

inbound_order_created.title: inbound_order_created
inbound_order_created.description: We capture inbound_order_created because we need to know how much stock enters each warehouse per day and who records it, which allows us to size receiving staff per warehouse and detect days with no receipts.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: `userId` in the envelope is the only person reference; no names or emails.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

outbound_order_created.title: outbound_order_created
outbound_order_created.description: We capture outbound_order_created because we need to know how many outbound orders are registered per day, per warehouse and per user, which allows us to plan picking capacity and replenishment.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

drained_to_zero.description: True when this order emptied the product.

order_validation_failed.title: order_validation_failed
order_validation_failed.description: We capture order_validation_failed because we need to know which products and fields accumulate the most validation errors, and how large the stock shortfall is, which allows us to fix confusing forms, correct stock records, or reorder products that operators keep over-requesting.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

product_id.description: Product UUID if it was a valid UUID.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

requested_quantity.description: Quantity requested, null if not an integer.

available_stock.description: Stock at refusal time, null if the product was not found.

shortfall.description: requested - available when insufficient_stock, else null.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.title: direct_stock_edit_rejected
direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: We capture direct_stock_edit_rejected because we need to know whether users or integrations try to bypass the inbound/outbound rule, and who, which allows us to decide on user training, tighter access, or a clearer UI when the attempts concentrate on one user or client.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

route_template.description: Route pattern such as `/inventory/products/{id}`, never the raw path.

rejected_fields.description: Allow-listed stock-like field names found in the payload (names only, never values).

product_id.description: Target product when present in the path.

client_app.description: Which client made the call, from the `X-Client-App` header.

stock_threshold_triggered.title: stock_threshold_triggered
stock_threshold_triggered.description: We capture stock_threshold_triggered because we need to know when and where the minimum-stock alerts fire most, which allows us to set reorder points and trigger replenishment before a warehouse stocks out.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

threshold_max_units.description: Upper bound of the band (0 or 9, the documented display thresholds).

triggering_order_id.description: Outbound order that caused the crossing.

stock_availability_checked.title: stock_availability_checked
stock_availability_checked.description: We capture stock_availability_checked because we need to know how often operators work against stale stock and how slow the check feels, which allows us to decide whether to poll, cache or push stock to the form.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

inventory_lock_wait_recorded.title: inventory_lock_wait_recorded
inventory_lock_wait_recorded.description: We capture inventory_lock_wait_recorded because we need to know whether concurrent operators contend on the same product, which allows us to decide if hot products need a different concurrency strategy.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

stock_snapshot_recorded.title: stock_snapshot_recorded
stock_snapshot_recorded.description: We capture stock_snapshot_recorded because we need to know how stock evolves over time, because stock is derived and has no history, which allows us to forecast demand, slow movers and seasonal replenishment.

x-trackflow.piiHandling: No personal data beyond the pseudonymous `userId` in the envelope.

sku.description: Product SKU (business identifier, not personal data).

login_succeeded.title: login_succeeded
login_succeeded.description: We capture login_succeeded because we need to know daily active users and which client apps are used, which allows us to prioritise the backoffice or website and size support.

login_failed.title: login_failed
login_failed.description: We capture login_failed because we need to know how many failed login attempts happen per day and whether they concentrate on one identifier, which allows us to tune rate limiting, add lockout or investigate credential-stuffing.

client_app.description: Which client made the call, from the `X-Client-App` header.

session_expired.description: We capture session_expired because we need to know how often operators lose a session mid-task, which allows us to adjust `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` or add silent renewal.
